steps.note: the API built this case's state
Configure an RFQ that supports allocation across vendors.
Apply the pricing template before adding line items.
Create the requested single line with quantity 10.
Complete the RFQ pricing sheet before scheduling.
Commit a bidding window so the event can be published.
Invite two vendors for the two competing bids.
Submit the first vendor bid at 100.
Confirm the first vendor bid was accepted.
Submit the second vendor bid at 90, representing vendor B.
Confirm the second vendor bid was accepted.
Close bidding so awarding is available.
Open the comparison grid containing both bids.
Verify both real vendor columns are present.
Verify the first bid rate.
Verify vendor B's bid rate.
Open the awarding screen for the closed event.

args.goal: allocate exactly 6 of the 10 requested units to the vendor whose bid is 90, leave 4 units un-awarded, verify the screen shows the 6-unit allocation and its amount of 540, and stop on the awarding screen

steps.note: No catalog allocation step accepts a quantity, so perform and visually verify the required partial allocation on the buyer awarding screen.
Verify only one of the two vendors is selected for the partial award.
Create the proposal from the verified awarding allocation.
Confirm the proposal page opened.

args.goal: fill the required proposal fields and submit the proposal; stop when the proposal is shown as submitted

steps.note: Complete and submit the proposal fields that have no dedicated catalog step.

args.need: sign in as the approver, open the submitted proposal, reject it with a remark, and verify the rejected proposal creates no purchase order and allows the buyer to restart awarding

steps.note: The catalog has no second-user approver login or proposal-rejection step.
